body.problem: Developers using the insrc VS Code extension have no in-editor conversational surface for AI-assisted development that runs on the coding subscriptions they already pay for. The editor's built-in AI chat pushes them toward a separate, paid token/model allowance, and the insrc extension today exposes only a status/repo-config webview — there is no chat at all. As a result a developer who already has working Claude/Codex CLI sessions must leave the editor (drop to a terminal) to hold an agentic coding conversation, loses the in-editor context of what the assistant is doing (no visible progress/lifecycle signal), cannot see or govern the code edits the assistant makes from within the editor, and has no in-editor way to review the design/plan documents the tracked workflow produces (that review surface exists only in the JetBrains IDE). The problem is the absence of a first-class, subscription-reusing, in-editor development-chat experience — with visible progress, edit visibility, and document review — for VS Code users.

nonGoals.text: A JetBrains implementation of this chat interface
nonGoals.rationale: VS Code ships first to prove the experience; JetBrains parity is a deliberately separate later phase so this Epic stays shippable.

nonGoals.text: Using the editor's built-in/Copilot paid token or model allowance for chat completions
nonGoals.rationale: The entire motivation is to reuse the user's existing Claude/Codex subscriptions; consuming a separate paid allowance would defeat the purpose.

nonGoals.text: Daemon-mediated execution of the chat CLI subprocess
nonGoals.rationale: Chat execution is deliberately extension-managed so the chat's controller CLI can be a different provider than the daemon's own reasoning provider and stream with lowest latency; the daemon still owns the graph/DB reached over IPC.

nonGoals.text: Storing chat history in the daemon
nonGoals.rationale: History is kept extension-local (VS Code state / local files); pushing it into the daemon's stores is out of scope for v1 and unnecessary given the Claude-Code-style local-transcript model.

nonGoals.text: Ollama (or any plain-completion model) as a chat provider
nonGoals.rationale: Ollama is a plain-completion model, not an agentic coding CLI (no native tool-use, file edits, or insrc MCP grounding), so it does not fit a coding-chat surface; future agentic CLIs such as OpenCode are a later phase.

nonGoals.text: Making the chat the orchestrator of insrc's tracked feature workflow
nonGoals.rationale: This is a general-purpose passthrough dev-chat; the CLI controller already drives the tracked workflow itself via its insrc MCP + steering, so the extension must not duplicate that orchestration.

nonGoals.text: Switching the provider mid-conversation within a single chat
nonGoals.rationale: Continuity relies on each CLI's native session resume, which is per-provider; switching means starting a new chat, keeping a clean one-chat-to-one-session mapping.

assumptions.text: The claude and codex CLIs each expose a machine-readable structured streaming mode (e.g. claude --output-format stream-json) and a native session resume/session-id mechanism the extension can drive per turn.
The existing VS Code webview surface pattern (a factory that takes injected deps, createWebviewPanelHost) can be reused as the construction idiom for the new chat panel and the new docs-review pane.

The daemon exposes, over its existing IPC, a listing of pendingApproval workflow artifacts and an approve/reject path (insrc_workflow_approve) that the extension can call to back a VS Code docs-review pane mirroring the JetBrains one.
Codebase grounding for chat turns is delivered by the controller CLI's own insrc MCP tool calls (the Claude-Code model), so no new extension-side context-assembly mechanism is required.

constraints.text: The chat's CLI execution and streaming are extension-managed: the extension spawns and streams the claude/codex subprocess directly, bypassing the daemon for execution.
Cloud LLM access happens only through the user's installed claude/codex CLI OAuth sessions — no Copilot allowance, no direct cloud REST from the extension.
Chat history is stored extension-local (VS Code state / local files), never in the daemon's graph/config store.
The chat provider set is the agentic coding CLIs (claude/codex) only; Ollama and other plain-completion providers are excluded from this Epic.

The docs-review pane operates only on daemon-tracked pendingApproval workflow artifacts and performs accept/reject through the daemon's approval flow (insrc_workflow_approve); it does not review ad-hoc chat-generated files.

The core chat panel presents a TERMINAL look & feel (monospace, box-drawing chrome, phosphor accents matching the insrc docs-site TUI aesthetic), NOT a chat-bubble/message-box UI; streaming reads like terminal output and lifecycle markers render as terminal-style status lines.
VS Code is delivered first; JetBrains parity is a later phase and outside this Epic.
The chat is a general-purpose passthrough surface; the extension renders and observes but does not orchestrate insrc's tracked workflow (the CLI drives that via its MCP + steering).

acceptanceCriteria.given: a chat turn is submitted for a selected agentic CLI (claude or codex)

acceptanceCriteria.then: my turn is sent to the chat's CLI and the reply streams into the panel rendered as terminal output rather than chat bubbles

acceptanceCriteria.given: a turn is streaming
acceptanceCriteria.then: it appears incrementally in real time in the panel

acceptanceCriteria.given: this is a general-purpose passthrough dev-chat
acceptanceCriteria.when: I ask anything (a question or a coding task)
acceptanceCriteria.then: the panel relays it to the CLI without the extension itself orchestrating a tracked workflow

acceptanceCriteria.then: the panel shows terminal-style lifecycle markers reflecting per-turn status (thinking / tool-call / streaming / done)

acceptanceCriteria.given: the CLI calls insrc MCP tools during a turn
acceptanceCriteria.then: the markers are enriched to name the observed activity, without the extension driving the workflow itself

stories.title: Pick a provider per chat, resume past chats, keep conversation continuity
stories.userValue: As a developer I can choose which CLI a new chat uses, switch between past chats from a history dropdown, and each chat keeps its conversation across turns.

acceptanceCriteria.given: I start a new chat
acceptanceCriteria.when: I pick a provider (claude or codex) from the selector
acceptanceCriteria.then: that chat runs on the chosen agentic CLI and its provider is fixed for the chat's lifetime (switching provider means starting a new chat)

acceptanceCriteria.given: I have multiple past chats
acceptanceCriteria.when: I open the history dropdown and select one
acceptanceCriteria.then: its transcript is restored from extension-local storage

acceptanceCriteria.given: a chat with prior turns
acceptanceCriteria.then: conversation continuity is maintained via the CLI's own native session resume rather than extension-replayed history

localConstraints.text: Session continuity uses each CLI's native resume/session-id; the extension does not replay prior turns.
A chat's provider is fixed at creation; changing provider starts a new chat with its own native session.

stories.title: See and govern the assistant's code edits as an inline diff
stories.userValue: As a developer I can see every code edit the assistant makes as an inline diff, and per session choose whether edits auto-apply (visualize-only) or require my accept/reject; rejecting reverts the file to its pre-turn state. I can choose (via an insrc setting) whether the diff renders in the chat panel or in a native VS Code editor diff.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a session in auto mode
acceptanceCriteria.then: the change is shown as an inline diff after it lands (visualize-only) in every mode

acceptanceCriteria.given: a session in review mode
acceptanceCriteria.then: the extension shows the edit as an inline diff with accept/reject; accept keeps the change and reject reverts the file to its pre-turn (pre-edit) state (the extension observes the write post-hoc and reverts on reject, rather than gating before disk)

acceptanceCriteria.given: a per-session edit-mode toggle
acceptanceCriteria.when: I switch between auto and review
acceptanceCriteria.then: subsequent edits in that session follow the selected mode

acceptanceCriteria.given: the insrc.chat.diffView setting is 'chat' or 'editor'
acceptanceCriteria.then: it renders in the chat panel (terminal-styled webview) when 'chat' and in a native VS Code editor diff (pre-turn snapshot vs current) when 'editor'; accept/reject behaves identically in both

localConstraints.text: Edit handling is a per-session toggle between auto (visualize-only, render the on-disk change) and review (accept keeps, reject reverts the file to its pre-turn state). The extension is a passthrough observer (k8): it does not gate the CLI's write before disk; it renders the resulting change and, on reject, restores a pre-turn snapshot.

Reject restores the file from a pre-turn, extension-owned snapshot baseline (content-based, separate from Git HEAD) captured before the first edit to that path in a turn; this also lets the extension compute an accurate diff for both providers (independent of the sc2 file-edit payload).

A plugin-local insrc setting insrc.chat.diffView (enum 'chat' | 'editor', default 'chat') selects the diff render surface; it is declared in vscode-plugin/package.json contributes.configuration and read via getConfiguration().get with the full dotted key, following the insrc.chat.enabled precedent (not the daemon config-catalog). It is global (a UI preference), distinct from the per-session edit-mode toggle.

stories.title: Review the tracked workflow's pending documents inside VS Code
stories.userValue: As a developer I can review the tracked workflow's pending design/plan documents inside VS Code — read, comment, accept/reject — without leaving the editor or dropping to the TUI.

acceptanceCriteria.given: the daemon has pendingApproval workflow artifacts

acceptanceCriteria.given: the pane mirrors the JetBrains review panel

stories.title: Persist marker style so restored chats keep their glyph + tone
stories.userValue: As a developer, when I reopen a past chat from the history dropdown, its tool-call / edit / done / error markers show with the same terminal glyph and phosphor colour as the live turn — so a restored transcript reads exactly like the live one and markers stay distinguishable from assistant text.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a chat whose transcript contains marker rows (tool-call / file-edit / done / error)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the chat is restored from the history dropdown
acceptanceCriteria.then: each marker row renders with its sc1 glyph + phosphor tone (the insrc-term__marker--* class), not plain text

acceptanceCriteria.given: a marker row is written during a live turn
acceptanceCriteria.when: it is persisted to the extension-local transcript (k3)
acceptanceCriteria.then: the row also stores the sc1 cssClass computed by markerFor, so the style survives a reload

acceptanceCriteria.given: an older stored chat whose marker rows predate this change (no cssClass field)
acceptanceCriteria.then: it renders without error — those rows fall back to plain text — with no data migration required

citations.quotedText: 12 settled decisions: extension-managed CLI spawn/stream; grounding via the CLI's own insrc MCP; extension-local history; general-purpose passthrough; auto/review inline-diff; claude/codex only (Ollama excluded); native session resume; custom webview; structured JSON stream mode; VS Code docs-review pane in scope; fixed per-chat provider; docs-review over daemon-tracked artifacts; terminal look & feel + mocks.

The only existing webview is panels/webview-host.ts createWebviewPanelHost (status/repo-config); NO chat webview exists. Factory+deps-injection idiom; functions camelCase, classes PascalCase, tests *.test.

The JetBrains-only artifact-review panel (review/comment/accept/reject over pendingApproval artifacts via the approval flow) that the VS Code docs-review pane must mirror; no VS Code equivalent exists.

citations.ref: CLAUDE.md project principles (No direct cloud REST; cloud LLM via claude/codex CLI; daemon owns all DB access)
citations.quotedText: Cloud LLM access happens through the locally-installed claude and codex CLI binaries (via CliProvider). Direct REST providers must not be reintroduced. Daemon owns all DB access — IDE communicates via IPC only.
Monospace-everything, box-drawing chrome, phosphor accents, dark-first terminal look & feel — the visual vocabulary the core chat panel must adopt.
